The bug in [`Partial.with(DateTimeFieldType, int)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L426-L474) has been resolved.

### Root Cause
In [`Partial.with(DateTimeFieldType, int)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L464), the package-private constructor `Partial(Chronology, DateTimeFieldType[], int[])` was being called instead of the validating public constructor `Partial(DateTimeFieldType[], int[], Chronology)`. The package-private constructor only assigns fields without validation, allowing conflicting or duplicate fields (such as `clockhourOfDay` when `hourOfDay` is already present) to be added without throwing an `IllegalArgumentException`.

### Changes Made
- Modified [`src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/Partial.java#L464) to invoke `new Partial(newTypes, newValues, iChronology)`.
- Generated the focused patch file [`negative_fix.patch`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_4_group_c_fix/negative_fix.patch).
- Ran the verification test `CucumberTest`, which passed successfully.
